title: Reported Speech — Introduction
description: Learn reported (indirect) speech for Grade 7: changing statements, questions and commands, with tense back-shift, pronoun and time changes — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Reporting Statements — Tense, Pronoun & Time Changes
topics.concept:
To report a statement, drop the quotation marks, add that, and shift the tense one step into the past (if the reporting verb is past).

Direct tenseReported tense
Simple presentSimple past
Present continuousPast continuous
Present perfect / Simple pastPast perfect
will / can / maywould / could / might

Pronouns change to match the new speaker (I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her).

Time and place words change: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there, this → that.

Exception: a universal truth stays in the present — The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.

examples.problem: Report: He said, "I will help you tomorrow."
examples.solution: He said that he would help me the next day. — 'will'→'would', 'tomorrow'→'the next day'.

recap: Add 'that' and shift the tense one step back
Change pronouns to match the new speaker

topics.title: Reporting Questions & Commands
topics.concept:
Questions: change the reporting verb to asked (or enquired), and turn the question into a statement (no inversion, no question mark).

  • Yes/No questions use if / whether: He asked, "Are you ready?" → He asked if I was ready.
  • Wh- questions keep the wh- word: She asked, "Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.

Commands and requests: use a reporting verb like told, ordered, asked, requested, advised + to + verb (infinitive).

  • "Sit down," he said. → He told me to sit down.
  • "Please help me," she said. → She requested me to help her.
  • Negative command: "Don't run." → He told me not to run.

examples.solution: He asked if I liked tea. — yes/no question uses 'if', verb shifts to 'liked'.
The teacher told us to open our books. — command → told + infinitive.

recap: Yes/No → if/whether; Wh- → keep the wh- word
Commands → told/asked + to + verb (negative: not to + verb)

questions.q: 'am' becomes ___ in reported speech.
Report: 'She said, "I can swim."'
options: She said that I could swim.

questions.q: Report: 'He said, "Don't shout."'
options: He told me not to shout.
He told me to not shouting.
questions.explanation: Negative command → told + not to + verb.

questions.q: 'tomorrow' becomes:
Report: 'She asked, "Are you tired?"'
options: She asked if I was tired.
She asked that I was tired.
She asked if was I tired.

questions.q: 'do' (simple present) becomes:
Report: 'He said, "I am reading."'
options: He said that I was reading.

questions.q: A command is reported using:
'here' changes to:
Report: 'She said, "I have finished."'
Report: 'He asked, "What is your name?"'
options: He asked what my name was.
He asked what was my name.
He asked that what my name was.
He asked what is my name.

questions.q: Which reporting verb suits a request?
Report: 'The guide said, "The museum opens at nine."'
options: The guide said the museum opened at nine.
The guide said the museum opens at nine.
Both are acceptable (a permanent fact may stay present).
The guide said the museum had opened at nine.
questions.explanation: A general/permanent fact may keep the present tense or back-shift; both are accepted.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'He asked me that whether I would help.'
Report: 'She said, "Let's go for a walk."' (suggestion)
options: She suggested going for a walk.
She said let us go for a walk.
She told to go for a walk.
She asked to go for a walk.

questions.q: Choose the correct report: 'He said, "I must leave now."'
options: He said he must leave then.
He said he had to leave then.
He said he musted leave now.
He said that leave now he must.

questions.q: Report: 'Mother said, "May God bless you!"' (a wish)
options: Mother prayed that God might bless me.
Mother said God may bless me.
Mother told God to bless me.
Mother asked if God blessed me.
questions.explanation: A wish/prayer is reported with 'prayed/wished that … might'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'The teacher told that we should be quiet.'
questions.explanation: 'told' needs an object ('told us'), or use 'said that'.

questions.q: Report the exclamation: 'He said, "What a beautiful sight!"'
options: He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful sight.
He said what a beautiful sight.
He asked what a beautiful sight it was.
He told that it was beautiful sight.
questions.explanation: Exclamations are reported with 'exclaimed that … very …'.

questions.q: Choose the correct report: 'She said, "I have been waiting since morning."'
options: She said she has been waiting since morning.
She said she had been waiting since that morning.
She said that I had been waiting.
She said she waited since morning.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous; 'morning' adjusted to 'that morning'.

outcomes: Tell direct speech apart from reported (indirect) speech
Change statements into reported speech with tense back-shift
Change pronouns and time/place words appropriately

intro.en: When we repeat someone's words exactly, with quotation marks, that is direct speech. When we report the meaning in our own words, without quotation marks, that is reported (indirect) speech. Changing one to the other follows clear rules — for tense, pronouns and time words.
intro.hi: जब हम किसी के शब्द हू-ब-हू, उद्धरण-चिह्नों के साथ दोहराते हैं, वह प्रत्यक्ष कथन (direct speech) है। जब हम अर्थ अपने शब्दों में, बिना उद्धरण-चिह्नों के बताते हैं, वह अप्रत्यक्ष कथन (reported/indirect speech) है। एक को दूसरे में बदलने के स्पष्ट नियम हैं — काल, सर्वनाम और समय-शब्दों के लिए।

real_life.situation:
You pass on a message:

Direct: Riya said, "I am busy today."

Reported: Riya said that she was busy that day.
real_life.why: Notice three changes: 'I' became 'she' (pronoun), 'am' became 'was' (tense back-shift), and 'today' became 'that day' (time word). These three changes are the core of reported speech.

rule_box.formula: Reporting verb (past) + that + clause with one tense back-shift
rule_box.example: He said, "I will come." → He said that he would come.

quick_test.q: In reported speech, a yes/no question is introduced by:
quick_test.explanation: Yes/No questions in reported speech use 'if' or 'whether'.

common_mistakes.wrong: She said that she is tired.
common_mistakes.note: Shift the tense back after a past reporting verb.

common_mistakes.wrong: He asked that where I lived.
common_mistakes.note: Don't use 'that' with a wh- question.

common_mistakes.wrong: He asked if was I ready.

fill_l1.instructions: Change the verb to its reported (back-shifted) form.

items.answer: She said that she was happy.
He said that he would call me.
She asked where I was going.
He told me to close the door.

items.q: "Do you like ice cream?" he asked.
items.answer: He asked if I liked ice cream.

error_detection.sentence: She said that she is tired.
error_detection.correct: She said that she was tired.

error_detection.sentence: He asked that where I lived.
She asked if was I coming.
error_detection.correct: She asked if I was coming.

sentence_correction.wrong: He said that he will come tomorrow.
sentence_correction.correct: He said that he would come the next day.

sentence_correction.wrong: She asked me that what I wanted.
sentence_correction.correct: She asked me what I wanted.

sentence_correction.wrong: The teacher told open the books.
sentence_correction.correct: The teacher told us to open the books.

rearrangement.jumbled: tired / she / was / said / that / she
rearrangement.answer: She said that she was tired.

reading.passage: Before the trip, the teacher gave instructions. She said that the bus would leave at seven and told everyone to be on time. "Do you have your permission slips?" she asked. Rahul replied that he had brought his. "Don't forget your water bottles," she added, reminding us to stay hydrated.

questions.q: Rewrite 'the bus would leave at seven' in direct speech.
questions.answer: She said, "The bus will leave at seven."

questions.q: How is the yes/no question reported?
questions.answer: It would become: She asked if we had our permission slips ('if' + statement order).

questions.q: Find a negative command reported in the passage.
questions.answer: "Don't forget your water bottles" → reported as telling/reminding us not to forget our water bottles.

speaking: She said that she was busy.
He told me to wait outside.
They asked where the station was.
I said that I would help.
The guard asked if we had tickets.

writing.prompt: Write a short conversation in direct speech (3 lines), then rewrite all of it in reported speech.
writing.example: Direct: Mum said, "Dinner is ready." Reported: Mum said that dinner was ready.

options: She said that she is ill.
She said that she was ill.
He said to open the window.
He told me to open the window.
He said that open the window.

micro_quiz.q: A wh- question is reported with:
micro_quiz.explanation: Keep the wh- word (where, what, why).

challenge.q: Report correctly: 'He said, "I saw her yesterday."'
options: He said that he saw her yesterday.
He said that he had seen her the previous day.
He said that he has seen her yesterday.
He said he sees her the day before.
challenge.explanation: Simple past → past perfect; 'yesterday' → 'the previous day'.

options: She asked why was I crying.
She asked why I was crying.
She asked that why I was crying.
She asked why I am crying.

challenge.q: Which keeps the present tense in reported speech?
options: He said the earth moves around the sun.
challenge.explanation: A universal truth does not back-shift.
